messages:
maya: thinking through a rollout for a new 'tiered_fallback_v2' flow — tenant-tiered canary that prefers high-quality model, but auto-fails to a quantized low-cost path based on latency/error/cost signals. want to align on flags, success metrics, and quick rollback criteria.

sam: sounds good. are we doing percent-based canaries or tenant cohorts (aka by plan)?

maya: plan is hybrid — 1) 1% global percent for public canary, 2) 5 pilot tenants (mid+enterprise) for tenant-cohort canary, and 3) opt-in beta for a handful of startups.

liam: telemetry we need: p95 latency, error-rate (5xx / decode errors), cost-per-request, and token-usage delta. also need per-tenant traces to see KV cache hitrate.

maya: agreed. primary success metrics: p95 <= baseline + 20ms, error-rate delta < 0.05%, cost-per-token delta < 10% for canary group.

sam: concrete abort criteria: p95 > baseline + 50ms for 5 minutes OR error-rate > baseline + 0.5% for 3 min OR token-cost increase > 20% sustained for 10 min.

maya: adding kill-switch: feature_flag = "tiered_fallback_v2" with subflags: 
```
{ 
  "tiered_fallback_v2.enabled": true,
  "tiered_fallback_v2.mode": "percent|tenant|optin",
  "tiered_fallback_v2.percent": 1,
  "tiered_fallback_v2.tenants": ["pilot-a","pilot-b"],
  "tiered_fallback_v2.fallback_policy": "quantize_then-region-fallback"
}
```

tess: do we need different rollout for Dedicated customers? they often have stricter latency SLAs.

maya: yes — Dedicated will default to no auto-fallback; instead we'll expose a controlled canary route that SRE can opt into per-pool. the flag will be able to include "disable_auto_fallback" per-tenant.

liam: ops checklist: 
- dashboard per-flag with p95, errors, cost delta
- alert rules matching abort criteria (pager for enterprise, slack for devs)
- synthetic traffic hitting the canary variant to validate steady-state

sam: can we A/B test quality too? e.g., 1% gets fallback logic but keeps higher-quality model for evaluation (shadow) to surface quality regressions.

maya: yes — shadowing plan: keep primary path on fallback but mirror outputs to the HQ model asynchronously for eval. surface BLEU/EMB similarity + custom prompt tests.

liam: timeline?

maya: this week: infra + dashboards wired. next Tue: internal canary (1% global) for 24h. Wed: tenant pilots. Fri: enable opt-in beta. plan to keep canary at 1% for 72h with rolling checks.

sam: naming convention for flags/variants? please avoid long names. propose: `tiered_fallback.v2` + variants `v2.percent`, `v2.tenants`, `v2.mode`.

maya: fine. also adding policy for fallbacks: priority list = [local-quantized, regional-standard, hosted-compat]. fallback decision will consider latency+cost+data residency.

liam: need a runbook snippet for ops when fallback oscillates:
```
1) Check cache-miss rates and model load on GPU nodes
2) If oscillation for single tenant -> mute flag for tenant
3) If global oscillation -> ramp down percent to 0.1% and engage SRE
4) If cost spike -> force fallback to quantized across canary
```

sam: one more ask — add a transparent billing note for customers in pilot: show expected token-cost delta in console so CSMs can explain tradeoffs.

maya: good. I'll open the PR for flag definitions + dashboard templates. tagging owners: @sam for alerts, @liam for runbook, @tess for customer comms.

deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: feature_flags/tiered_fallback_v2 -> rollout-plan/4260000000/init (dry-run)

maya: thanks. will post a short status update in #customer-ops when internal canary starts. :thumbsup:

tess: I'll prep a short FAQ for pilot tenants about what to expect and the opt-out path.

sam: approved on abort criteria from SRE side.

liam: on call for Wed tenant pilot window.

maya: perfect — closing the loop. we'll sync after 24h with concrete telemetry snapshots.
